body:
Supersedes d-kit's 'vendor and patch' plan and closes q-forks part 1. On NixOS a shim is not PATH archaeology: the wrapper *is* the package, installed by overlay or module, with the raw binary always addressable as ${pkgs.zmx}/bin/zmx. Nothing is monkeypatched, nothing depends on PATH order, and the behaviour change is declarative, visible in the derivation and revertible in one line.

The wrapper owns three rewrites and passes everything else through untouched:
1. attach (create): compute `project.id` → `project`/`id` labels, add `--labels` to the same `zmx attach` call (labels are create-time only, so this must be one call), and exec through the launcher prefix (systemd-run --user --scope --collect --quiet) when it is usable.
2. run (dispatch): same naming and creation rewrite, plus `state=working` before the real `zmx run` and `state=done`/`failed` after, exiting with the task's own code. The wrapper is the dispatcher here, which is exactly the party d-state-writer allows to write state.
3. Nothing else. ls/get/set/send/print/write/history/wait/tail/kill/detach/version pass through verbatim.

Consequences: zp and pi-zmx need no fork at all — zp's `zmx attach` and pi-zmx's `zmx run <name> true` inherit naming, labels, durable birth and state by being callers of the wrapped zmx. The custom `zmux` verb disappears, and with it the 150 lines that were the plan's only new code. What remains is a wrapper, an elisp rewrite, a vocabulary document, tests and flake wiring.

Deliberate limits (c-wrapper-limits): only names with a dot get labels; an existing session is never relabelled; the raw binary stays one env var or one absolute path away; and `blocked` is not derivable here.
title: Ship a wrapped zmx, not a patched ecosystem and not a new binary
